problem: Let $f(t)=t\sqrt[3]{\operatorname{tan}⁡t}.$ Find ${g}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})$ given the function $g$ is defined by $g(x)={\int }_{0}^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t$ for $0<x<\frac{\pi }{2}.$
worked_solution:
The function $f(t)=t\sqrt[3]{\operatorname{tan}⁡t}$ is continuous on $[0,x],$ where $0<x<\frac{\pi }{2}.$ So, FTC II applies, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}{\int }_{0}^{x}t\sqrt[3]{\operatorname{tan}⁡t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =x\sqrt[3]{\operatorname{tan}⁡x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the value of ${g}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}),$ we substitute $x=\frac{\pi }{4}$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =\frac{\pi }{4}\sqrt[3]{\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{4}\sqrt[3]{1} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{4}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
